exam_name: ISTQB Certified Tester Test Automation Engineering

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: Which is a realistic objective of test automation?

options.A: To completely replace all manual testing
options.B: To improve efficiency, coverage, and repeatability of testing, and to give faster feedback
options.C: To guarantee the software has no defects
options.D: To remove the need for a test strategy

questions.explanation: Automation aims at efficiency, wider and repeatable coverage, and faster feedback. It complements rather than replaces manual and exploratory testing, and cannot prove absence of defects.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: In ISTQB terms, the SUT is the:

options.A: Software Under Test
options.B: System Uptime Tracker

questions.explanation: SUT stands for the software (or system) under test, the application that the test automation solution exercises.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: The abbreviation TAS in CTAL-TAE refers to the:

options.A: Test Automation Strategy
options.B: Test Automation Solution

questions.explanation: The TAS is the realised Test Automation Solution: the automation framework or tools plus the test environment and testware for a specific project.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: TAA in the CTAL-TAE syllabus stands for:

options.A: Test Automation Architecture
options.B: Test Analysis Approach

questions.explanation: The Test Automation Architecture (TAA) is the design of the automation framework; the generic version is the gTAA.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: Which factor most affects whether a given test is a good automation candidate?

options.A: The tester's favourite programming language
options.B: How often it will be run, its stability, and the effort to automate versus the value returned
options.C: The colour of the test report
options.D: The number of testers on the team

questions.explanation: Automation ROI depends on execution frequency, stability of the feature, and the automation effort relative to the benefit (regression protection, speed).

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: Which is a common limitation of test automation?

options.A: It can find defect types that require human judgement, such as usability problems
options.B: It cannot detect visual or usability issues the way a human tester can, and it requires ongoing maintenance
options.C: It never needs updating once written
options.D: It removes the need for test design

questions.explanation: Automated checks verify expected conditions but do not judge look-and-feel or exploratory concerns, and they incur maintenance cost as the SUT evolves.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation
questions.question: How does the SUT architecture influence tool selection?

options.A: It does not; any tool works with any SUT
options.B: The SUT's technologies, interfaces (UI, API, message bus), and testability features determine which tools can drive and observe it
options.C: Only the SUT's colour scheme matters
options.D: Tool selection depends solely on price

questions.explanation: A tool must be able to interact with the SUT's platforms and interfaces and read its outputs; testability hooks (IDs, APIs) strongly affect feasibility.

questions.question: "Testability" of the SUT for automation is improved by:

options.A: Removing all logging
options.B: Stable, unique identifiers for UI elements, APIs for setup/verification, and controllable state
options.C: Randomising element IDs on each build

questions.explanation: Automation is easier when the SUT exposes stable locators, control/observation points (APIs), and ways to set up and reset state deterministically.

questions.question: A pilot project for a new automation tool is mainly used to:

options.A: Deliver the whole regression suite in one week
options.B: Evaluate the tool against the SUT and process on a small scale before committing broadly

questions.explanation: A pilot validates tool fit, integration, and team capability on a limited scope, reducing the risk of a large-scale tool decision.

questions.question: Which is a key criterion when comparing candidate automation tools?

options.A: Compatibility with the SUT's technology stack and interfaces
options.B: Whether the vendor's office is nearby
options.D: The number of letters in the tool name

questions.explanation: Technical fit with the SUT is fundamental; other criteria include maintainability, reporting, CI integration, licensing, and required skills.

questions.question: Open-source automation tools compared with commercial tools typically:

options.A: Always have better vendor support
options.B: Have no licence cost but may need more in-house expertise and offer community rather than contractual support

questions.explanation: Open-source tools trade licence cost for a greater need for internal skills and reliance on community support, though many are widely used and CI-friendly.

questions.question: The gTAA (generic Test Automation Architecture) defines layers. Which is one of them?

options.A: The marketing layer
options.B: The test generation, test definition, test execution, and test adaptation layers

questions.explanation: The gTAA is structured into test generation, test definition, test execution, and test adaptation layers, promoting separation of concerns and reuse.

questions.question: The main purpose of the test adaptation layer is to:

options.A: Store test results in a spreadsheet
options.B: Connect the test cases to the various interfaces of the SUT (UI, API, protocols) via adapters

questions.explanation: The adaptation layer provides the adapters/drivers that let test definitions interact with the SUT's specific interfaces, isolating that dependency.

questions.question: In a keyword-driven framework, a keyword represents:

options.A: A reusable action or business step (for example "Login", "AddToCart") that hides the technical implementation
options.B: A password

questions.explanation: Keywords are named, reusable operations. Test cases are written as sequences of keywords, keeping tests readable and implementation details encapsulated.

questions.question: Data-driven testing separates:

options.A: The test logic from the test data, so the same script runs with many input sets
options.B: The testers from the developers
options.C: The UI from the database permanently

questions.explanation: In data-driven testing, one script is executed repeatedly with different data rows from an external source, improving coverage without duplicating scripts.

questions.question: The Page Object Model (POM) pattern helps automation maintainability by:

options.A: Putting all locators and page interactions for a screen in one class, so a UI change is fixed in one place
options.B: Deleting old test cases automatically
options.C: Making tests run without a browser

questions.explanation: POM encapsulates a page's elements and actions. Tests call page methods, so when the UI changes only the page object is updated.

questions.question: Capture/playback (record-and-replay) scripts are often criticised because they:

options.A: Are highly maintainable and readable
options.B: Tend to be brittle, hard to maintain, and full of hard-coded values and unstable locators
options.D: Always use the Page Object Model

questions.explanation: Recorded scripts capture low-level interactions and literal data, making them fragile and costly to maintain as the SUT changes.

questions.question: Behaviour-driven development (BDD) frameworks such as Cucumber express tests in:

options.A: Binary machine code
options.B: Given/When/Then scenarios in near-natural language, backed by step definitions

questions.explanation: BDD uses Gherkin's Given/When/Then structure so scenarios are readable by non-technical stakeholders, with step definitions providing the automation code.

questions.question: A "flaky" automated test is one that:

options.A: Always passes
options.B: Passes and fails intermittently without any change to the SUT or the test

questions.explanation: Flaky tests give non-deterministic results, undermining trust in the suite. Common causes include timing/synchronisation issues and shared state.

questions.question: A frequent cause of UI test flakiness is:

options.A: Using explicit waits for elements to be ready
options.B: Fixed sleeps and race conditions where the test acts before the application has finished updating

questions.explanation: Hard-coded sleeps and unsynchronised interactions cause intermittent failures. Explicit waits on conditions are the recommended fix.

questions.question: Which practice most reduces inter-test dependency problems?

options.A: Making each test set up its own data and not rely on the order or side effects of other tests
options.B: Sharing one global logged-in session across all tests
options.C: Running tests only in a fixed sequence

questions.explanation: Independent, self-contained tests can run in any order and in parallel, and a failure in one does not cascade into others.

questions.question: A risk of automating tests too early, before the UI or API is stable, is:

options.A: The tests will be perfectly stable
options.B: High rework/maintenance cost as the interface keeps changing

questions.explanation: Automating against a volatile interface means constant script churn. It is often better to stabilise the interface or automate at a more stable layer first.

questions.question: Which metric best reflects the value of an automated regression suite for fast feedback?

options.A: Number of lines in the test code
options.B: Suite execution time and the time from code commit to test result
options.C: Number of testers in the room

questions.explanation: Feedback speed, how quickly the suite runs and reports after a change, is a core value metric for CI automation.

questions.question: A good automated test report should primarily help the reader to:

options.A: Admire the formatting
options.B: Quickly see what passed, what failed, and enough detail (logs, screenshots, stack traces) to start diagnosis
options.C: Count the number of test files

questions.explanation: Reports exist to communicate results and speed up defect investigation, so failure context (evidence, logs) is essential.

questions.question: "Automation coverage" as a metric usually means:

options.A: The percentage of the office covered by Wi-Fi
options.B: The proportion of defined test cases or requirements that are covered by automated tests
options.C: The number of monitors per tester
options.D: How much disk the tool uses

questions.explanation: It expresses how much of the intended test scope (cases, requirements, or risks) is exercised by automation rather than only manually.

questions.question: Tracking the automated suite's pass rate trend over time helps to:

options.A: Detect a decline in SUT quality or a rise in flakiness/maintenance debt
options.B: Decide the lunch menu

questions.explanation: A falling or erratic pass rate signals product defects, environment problems, or growing test-maintenance debt that needs attention.

questions.domain: Transitioning Manual Testing to an Automated Environment
questions.question: When transitioning manual test cases to automation, which are usually automated first?

options.A: One-off, rarely repeated exploratory sessions
options.B: Stable, high-value, frequently executed regression cases
options.C: Tests that need constant human judgement
options.D: Tests for features scheduled for removal

questions.explanation: The best early candidates are stable, repetitive, high-value regression tests where automation quickly repays the effort.

questions.domain: Transitioning Manual Testing to an Automated Environment
questions.question: A manual test case being automated often needs to be:

options.A: Left completely vague
options.B: Made precise and deterministic, with explicit preconditions, data, steps, and expected results
options.C: Deleted from the test management tool

questions.explanation: Automation requires unambiguous, repeatable specifications: exact setup, data, actions, and verifiable expected outcomes.

questions.domain: Transitioning Manual Testing to an Automated Environment
questions.question: Which is a sensible expectation when introducing automation to a team?

options.A: Manual testing effort drops to zero immediately
options.B: There is an initial investment period before automation yields net time savings
options.D: The test strategy is no longer needed

questions.explanation: Building the framework and first tests costs effort up front; the payback comes from repeated executions over subsequent cycles.

questions.question: Why should the test automation code itself be reviewed and tested?

options.A: It is production software with its own defects that can cause false passes or false failures
options.B: Because reviews are mandatory for all documents

questions.explanation: Testware is code. Bugs in it can hide real defects (false pass) or waste time (false fail), so it needs the same quality practices as the SUT.

questions.question: A "false negative" in test automation refers to a test that:

options.A: Fails when the SUT is actually working correctly
options.B: Passes when the SUT is actually broken

questions.explanation: In common automation usage, a false negative (false alarm) is a failing test caused by the test/environment rather than a real SUT defect. A false positive is a passing test that misses a real defect.

questions.question: Checking that a new automated test actually fails when the behaviour it verifies is broken is a way to:

options.A: Confirm the test has genuine verification power (it is not a no-op assertion)
options.B: Increase execution time

questions.explanation: Deliberately breaking the behaviour (or the assertion) and seeing the test fail proves the test can detect the defect it claims to guard against.

questions.question: Integrating the automated suite into a CI pipeline means tests run:

options.A: Only once a year
options.B: Automatically on triggers such as each commit, merge, or scheduled build, giving fast feedback

questions.explanation: CI integration executes tests on defined triggers so regressions are caught close to the change that caused them.

questions.question: In a CI pipeline, a fast "smoke" or "sanity" automated suite is typically run:

options.A: Never
options.B: Early, to quickly reject builds with obvious breakage before longer suites run
options.C: Only manually by the release manager

questions.explanation: A short smoke suite gives rapid go/no-go feedback so the pipeline does not waste time running full regression on a fundamentally broken build.

questions.question: Continuous improvement of a TAS involves periodically:

options.A: Reviewing flaky tests, slow tests, duplicated code, and coverage gaps, and acting on them
options.B: Deleting the whole framework and starting again every sprint
options.C: Ignoring maintenance until the suite is unusable
options.D: Adding tests only, never removing any

questions.explanation: A healthy TAS is maintained: flakiness and slowness are addressed, dead or duplicate tests removed, and coverage gaps filled based on risk.

questions.question: "Contract testing" between services checks that:

options.A: The legal contract with the vendor is signed
options.B: A provider's API and a consumer's expectations of it stay compatible, without a full end-to-end environment
options.C: The UI colours match the brand

questions.explanation: Consumer-driven contract tests verify that each side of a service boundary honours the agreed request/response shape, catching integration breakage early and cheaply.

questions.question: Separating configuration (URLs, credentials, environment settings) from test code mainly helps to:

options.A: Run the same tests against different environments without changing the code
options.B: Make the tests longer
options.D: Stop the tests from running in CI

questions.explanation: Externalised configuration lets one test suite target dev, test, staging, or prod by swapping a config file or environment variables.

questions.question: Which role commonly leads the design of the Test Automation Architecture?

options.A: The Test Automation Engineer / Test Automation Architect
options.B: The office facilities manager

questions.explanation: The Test Automation Engineer (with an architect focus) designs and maintains the TAA/TAS, working with testers and developers.
